title: Reading errors and IFERROR
explanation: A merch shop's sheet is full of strange messages like **#DIV/0!**. These are **errors**: Excel's way of saying a formula can't give an answer. Each one has a meaning, and once you can read them, they're easy to fix or hide.

tasks.prompt: Click D3 and look at its error.
tasks.teach: The common errors: **#DIV/0!** means dividing by zero. **#NAME?** means Excel doesn't recognise a name, usually a misspelled function. **#VALUE!** means the wrong kind of data, like doing maths with text. **#N/A** means a lookup couldn't find a match (you'll meet it in Level 6). **#REF!** means a formula points at a cell that was deleted.
hints: Cap has 0 units, so it divides by zero.

tasks.prompt: Which kind of error is in D3? Type DIV/0 into H3 (without the # or !).
hints: The Cap sold 0 units, and you can't divide by 0.

tasks.prompt: H2 should add up the revenue, but it shows #NAME?. Click it and fix the misspelled function.
hints: SUM is spelled with one M.

tasks.prompt: In E2, work out the price per unit, but show "Check" instead of an error: =IFERROR(B2/C2, "Check"). Then copy it down to E7.
tasks.teach: **IFERROR(formula, if_error)** shows the formula's answer normally, but if it would be an error, it shows your message instead. It keeps reports clean. Use it carefully, though: hiding errors can hide real problems.
hints: Cap, Sticker and Socks should say Check.
tasks.answer: =IFERROR(B2/C2, "Check") in E2, then copy down to E7

tasks.prompt: Last one: Socks shows #VALUE! because its revenue is the text "n/a". The real revenue was 300. Fix B7, and watch D7, E7 and the total update.
hints: D7 and E7 become 30, and H2 becomes 1685.

recap: #DIV/0! is dividing by zero, #NAME? is a misspelled name, #VALUE! is the wrong kind of data, #N/A is a failed lookup, and #REF! is a deleted cell. IFERROR shows a message instead of an error.
